Differential expression: many comparisons

Source: vignettes/articles/de-multi.Rmd
de-multi.Rmd

Question: across several comparisons, how many genes change, which genes change where, and do two comparisons agree?

Function Shows Best for
plot_multi_volcano() the genes of each comparison, one column each the size and shape of each response
plot_de_dots() chosen genes × comparisons: fold change and significance specific genes across comparisons
plot_fc_quadrant() fold changes of one comparison against another whether two responses agree

All three read their input with standardize_de() (see DE: one comparison): a named list of DE tables (names are the comparisons), or one long table with a comparison column (comparison.col, e.g. "cluster" for Seurat::FindAllMarkers()).

As in the single-cell plots, the comparisons play the part of group.by (the units compared, marked by their colour) and the optional groups of comparisons (e.g. a lineage above its cell types) that of split.by: blocks marked by a bar and a name, black by default (groups.cols), opposite the comparison names (groups.side).

Data: interferon-β (IFN-β) vs control in each cell type of the PBMCs of Kang et al. 2018: counts summed per donor, condition and cell type (pseudobulk), edgeR quasi-likelihood test paired by donor, for the 6 cell types with at least 10 cells in every sample. Testing samples rather than cells avoids the inflated p-values of per-cell tests, which treat cells as replicates.

de <- docs_kang_de()
names(de)
#> [1] "CD4 T"       "CD8 T"       "NK"          "B"           "CD14 Mono"  
#> [6] "FCGR3A Mono"
# DE genes per cell type
vapply(de, function(t) sum(t$FDR < 0.05), integer(1))
#>       CD4 T       CD8 T          NK           B   CD14 Mono FCGR3A Mono 
#>        1392         228         461         565        2510        1057

Multi-comparison volcano

One column per comparison, marked by a strip of its colour and its name on top: genes at their log2 fold change, the up- and down-regulated ones each spread by their density, so the shape of each response shows; the non-significant genes spread evenly in light grey behind them; the cutoffs (±logfc.cutoff, default 1) as dashed lines; counts of up- and down-regulated genes above and below.

plot_multi_volcano(de)

CD14 monocytes respond with the most genes; the top genes of every cell type include interferon-stimulated genes. Colour is the −log10 adjusted p-value (warm for up, cool for down), saturating at the 95th percentile of the DE genes; each side of the colour bar ends at its own most significant gene, so the direction with weaker p-values is not faded.

Variants

A second level: comparisons of a group are drawn together, the group marked by a bar and its name at the bottom (groups.side = "labels" puts it at the top, beyond the comparison names).

lineage <- c(
    "CD4 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD8 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "NK" = "Lymphoid",
    "B" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD14 Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "FCGR3A Mono" = "Myeloid"
)
plot_multi_volcano(de, groups = lineage)

Comparisons as rows: down-regulated genes on the left, up-regulated on the right, the comparison names and strips on the left. comparison.cols takes a palette name, or colours named by comparison (e.g. the cell type colours of the embedding plots):

plot_multi_volcano(
    de,
    flip = TRUE,
    groups = lineage,
    comparison.cols = "okabe-ito",
    label.n = 2
)

"pvalue" places genes across their column by −log10 adjusted p-value, relative to the most significant gene on their side of 0 (each column is a sideways volcano). It suits bulk results, where thousands of non-significant genes would fill the column with grey in the default layout; "jitter" spreads all genes uniformly.

plot_multi_volcano(de, layout = "pvalue")

"sharing" colours genes by the number of comparisons they are DE in: responses shared by all cell types versus specific to one. "direction" uses one colour per direction.

plot_multi_volcano(de, color.by = "sharing", label = "none")

"n_de" puts the comparisons with the most DE genes first; "cluster" groups comparisons with similar fold-change profiles.

plot_multi_volcano(de, order = "cluster", label.n = 2)

A lower logfc.cutoff, and only the DE genes (show.ns = FALSE):

plot_multi_volcano(
    de,
    show.ns = FALSE,
    logfc.cutoff = 0.5,
    label = "none"
)

DE dot plot

Chosen genes across comparisons: colour is the log2 fold change, size the −log10 adjusted p-value, and non-significant results are faded. Each comparison is marked by a coloured dot, as the groups of the single-cell dot plot (comparison.marker = "dot", "strip" or "none"). Without features, the top n genes of each comparison:

plot_de_dots(de, n = 3)

The colour scale is centred on 0 and runs from the most negative to the most positive fold change of the significant dots, each side to its own full colour; give logfc.limits to share one scale between figures.

Variants

A named list of genes draws groups of columns, marked by bars on top (coloured with feature.group.cols):

genes <- list(
    "Interferon-stimulated" = c("ISG15", "IFI6", "IFIT1", "IFIT3", "MX1", "OAS1"),
    "Chemokines" = c("CXCL10", "CCL2", "CCL8")
)
plot_de_dots(de, features = genes)

"grey" draws non-significant results grey; "hide" leaves them out:

plot_de_dots(de, features = genes, significance = "grey")

Genes and comparisons ordered by clustering of their fold changes; genes as rows, comparisons as columns marked by colour strips:

plot_de_dots(
    de,
    n = 4,
    cluster.features = TRUE,
    cluster.comparisons = TRUE,
    flip = TRUE,
    comparison.marker = "strip"
)

Comparisons in groups of rows, each marked by a bar and its name (here in colour, beyond the comparison names):

plot_de_dots(
    de,
    features = genes,
    groups = lineage,
    groups.cols = c(Lymphoid = "#2C5DA8", Myeloid = "#B5338A"),
    groups.side = "labels"
)

Quadrant plot

The fold changes of two comparisons against each other. Genes significant in both are coloured by whether they change the same way: consistently up, consistently down, or in opposite directions (inconsistent); all others are grey. Counts of these genes in each quadrant, and the correlation of the fold changes above the panel. Do monocytes and B cells respond to IFN-β with the same genes?

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    label.n = 3
)

Most genes changed in both change in the same direction (top-right and bottom-left), and B cells respond to fewer genes, more weakly (the cloud lies below the diagonal on the right). “Consistent” needs significance in both comparisons: a gene significant in one only is among the others, whatever its sign in the other.

Variants

color.by = "direction" keeps only the consistent genes in colour (genes changed in opposite directions join the others, and only the top-right and bottom-left are counted). color.by = "significance" colours where each gene is significant: in both (same or opposite direction), in one only, or in neither.

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    color.by = "direction",
    label = "none"
)

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    color.by = "significance",
    label = "none"
)

A least-squares line of y on x, fitted on the genes of the correlation (cor.on), with a 95% band (trend.interval): “confidence” (default) shows where the fitted line lies, as geom_smooth(method = "lm") draws it, and is very narrow with many genes; “prediction” shows where 95% of the genes are expected to fall around the line. Both fold changes are noisy estimates, which biases a least-squares slope toward 0 (regression dilution): the line shows the trend, but its slope is not the ratio of the two responses.

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    cor.on = "significant",
    trend = TRUE,
    trend.interval = "prediction",
    label = "none"
)

The comparisons can come from different experiments, tools or designs. Here, macrophages (Alasoo et al. 2018) stimulated with IFN-γ or infected with Salmonella, each against naive, paired by donor. Fold change cutoffs are set per comparison (logfc.cutoff.x, logfc.cutoff.y; likewise padj.cutoff.x, padj.cutoff.y) and drawn as thin dashed lines:

mac <- docs_macrophage()
counts <- filter_low_expression_genes(mac$counts, min_group_size = 6)
y <- edgeR::normLibSizes(edgeR::DGEList(counts))
design <- model.matrix(~ donor + condition, data = mac$samples)
fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(y, design)
test_ifng <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionIFNg")
test_sl1344 <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionSL1344")
de_ifng <- edgeR::topTags(test_ifng, n = Inf)
de_sl1344 <- edgeR::topTags(test_sl1344, n = Inf)
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de_ifng,
    de_sl1344,
    name.x = "IFN-γ",
    name.y = "Salmonella",
    logfc.cutoff.x = 1,
    logfc.cutoff.y = 1
)

With color.by = "significance", colour only genes significant in both; correlation of the genes significant in either comparison:

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["CD4 T"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "CD4 T",
    color.by = "significance",
    categories = "both",
    cor.on = "significant",
    correlation = "pearson"
)

plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("ISG15", "CXCL10", "IFIT1", "MX1")
)

To compare RNA with chromatin (ATAC, ChIP, CUT&RUN), map the peaks of de.y to genes with map.y (e.g. from a ChIPseeker annotation); with several peaks per gene, the most significant one is used (map.summary). The peak table below is simulated from the monocyte RNA fold changes, only to show the input format:

rna <- de[["CD14 Mono"]]
set.seed(1)
genes_with_peaks <- sample(rownames(rna), 3000)
n_peaks <- sample(1:3, length(genes_with_peaks), replace = TRUE)
peak_gene <- rep(genes_with_peaks, n_peaks)
peak_logfc <- 0.5 * rna[peak_gene, "logFC"] + rnorm(length(peak_gene), sd = 0.6)
peaks <- data.frame(
    logFC = peak_logfc,
    row.names = paste0("peak_", seq_along(peak_gene))
)
peaks$PValue <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(peaks$logFC) / 0.4)
peaks$FDR <- p.adjust(peaks$PValue, "BH")
peak_to_gene <- data.frame(peak = rownames(peaks), gene = peak_gene)
head(peak_to_gene, 3)
#>     peak     gene
#> 1 peak_1 CYB561D2
#> 2 peak_2  PLEKHF2
#> 3 peak_3  PLEKHF2

plot_fc_quadrant(
    rna,
    peaks,
    name.x = "RNA",
    name.y = "ATAC (simulated)",
    map.y = peak_to_gene
)
